title: Composition-tuned Ti-BTC MOF/MoS 2  heterostructures for alkaline oxygen evolution electrocatalysis
content: The sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a major kinetic bottleneck for efficient alkaline water electrolysis, driving the need for robust electrocatalysts based on earth-abundant materials. Herein, we report composition-tuned titanium-based metal–organic framework (Ti-BTC MOF)/molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) heterostructures as efficient OER electrocatalysts by integrating a rarely explored titanium-based metal–organic framework (Ti-BTC) with benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylate (BTC) linkers with conductive flower-like MoS2 through a reflux-assisted in situ growth strategy. To establish the influence of catalyst composition, Ti-BTC/MoS2 heterostructures with different mass ratios were systematically synthesized and investigated. Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) surface-area analysis, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirm the successful formation of well-integrated heterostructures, while electrochemical measurements reveal a strong dependence of catalytic performance on composition. Among the investigated catalysts, the Ti-BTC/MoS2 (1 : 3) heterostructure exhibits the best OER activity, delivering an overpotential of 313 mV at 10 mA cm−2, a Tafel slope of 108 mV dec−1, lower charge-transfer resistance, a higher electrochemically accessible surface area (ECSA), and excellent operational stability over 50 h under alkaline conditions. The enhanced OER performance of TM13 is associated with its composition-dependent electrochemical behaviour, changes in the local chemical environments of the constituent elements, lower fitted charge-transfer resistance, and a larger estimated ECSA. These findings highlight the importance of composition tuning in regulating the electrochemical behaviour of Ti-BTC/MoS2 heterostructures and provide a basis for further investigation of titanium-based MOF composites for alkaline oxygen evolution.
